A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReCITE research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–Z support comparison; the reduction from 34 to 33 pages does not indicate missing material.

before.justification: v3 reports original model evaluations, node-name ablations, judge agreement analyses, and human and base-model case studies.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the ten-model benchmark comparison in Table 3 and name-assisted evaluation in Table 4.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction pipeline, graph-generation procedures, post-processing, and LLM-as-a-Judge framework are retained. Wording and prompt-formatting corrections do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 292-paper English benchmark, domain coverage, reference corpora, and standard and name-assisted tasks. Additional corpus statistics and model metadata do not expand evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated model sets, judge comparisons, TEA-GLM evaluation, and Qwen-2.5-7B base-model case study are retained. The base-model appendix is moved, and the new model-date table does not introduce comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 changes the stated explicitness grouping from four sections to three bins, matching the displayed bin count. Appendix E.1 changes its reported sample count from 290 to 292. Appendix G relabels unchanged median reasoning lengths from characters to tokens. These are reported protocol revisions; rerunning experiments is not established.

E4.justification: The explicitness analyses receive revised heatmaps and a replacement text-length scatterplot. Appendix H adds a node-count scatterplot and fit, while Appendix F adds journal and author diversity counts. Existing ablations, robustness checks, and case studies remain.

E5.justification: Standard-deviation reporting, correlation significance tests, rank-agreement statistics, and annotation-agreement reporting are retained. No new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or uncertainty-estimation practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Main Tables 3–5 remain unchanged, including the best F1 of 0.535. Appendix F swaps STEM/economics MMD values from 0.141/0.114 to 0.114/0.141 and adds 42 journals and 1,036 authors. Explicitness heatmaps change, and Figure 11 replaces the previously labeled strict plot, reporting R² = 0.171 instead of 0.169. New Figure 13 shows a negative fit with R² = 0.011, contradicting its caption's positive relationship and 0.002.

T1.justification: The lenient and strict explicitness equations, evaluation formulas, and scoring mathematics are retained. Revised explanations align the explicitness prose with existing equations rather than introducing new formal definitions, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same benchmark novelty claim, best-model F1 of 0.535, causal-reasoning bottleneck claim, and conclusion that lower explicitness increases difficulty.

C2.justification: Appendix K clarifies strict versus lenient explicitness and reframes the analysis as supporting explicitness's role in difficulty, replacing its claimed validation of automated labeling. Figure 9 drops the interpretation that QwQ's distribution reflects structured handling of reasoning chains. The stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Table 7 documents model release dates and knowledge cutoffs. The graph-statistics caption newly discloses edge deduplication. v4 also removes the footnote promising full dataset release upon publication while retaining the same code/data link; actual availability cannot be verified from these PDFs.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against previous benchmarks remain the same. Changes to author attribution, capitalization, citation formatting, and reference ordering are bibliographic cleanup.

P1.justification: v4 makes sentence-level copyedits, terminology and cross-reference corrections, and a localized rewrite of Appendix K. The base-model and human-expert appendices exchange positions, but the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 7 and the node-count plot, revises explicitness heatmaps and Figure 11, and gives the existing base-model screenshot a numbered caption. Other figures, tables, and prompt blocks are relocated or reflowed within the retained two-column design.

improvement.justification: v4 clarifies explicitness definitions, repairs several presentation inconsistencies, and adds useful reproducibility disclosures. However, new Figure 13 contradicts its caption, and Table 20 relabels DeepSeek R1's unchanged 22K median as tokens despite the retained Figure 10 distribution lying predominantly below 8K tokens. These introduced reporting problems coexist with useful corrections, leaving the net quality effect uncertain.
